## 3. What is selling
**For:** Rank products and plans by sales, units and orders; include available product links and publication status.

**Connection pattern:** Metorik product report → Markdown → collected with the other reports → delivery. Published status does not verify the live checkout.

Last 7 completed days • timezone and currency from Settings

## PRIVATE CONNECTION TEMPLATE
All HTTP and delivery nodes are disabled; credentials removed. Fill in the Settings node and credentials before enabling HTTP nodes. Until a source is connected, its lane writes an INCOMPLETE report instead of stopping the run.

Real requests expose real data in execution outputs. Do not execute on a public screen. Use the demo for the workshop.

Switch on a delivery node only after choosing your own destination and reviewing the reports.

parameters.content:
## 4. Website traffic review (GA4)
**For:** traffic quality, channel mix, landing pages and purchase/lead events. Last 7 completed days vs prior 7.
**Demo:** fictional GA4 response → review → Markdown file → collected with the other reports → delivery (switched off).
**Real connection:** select GA4 OAuth and property ID in Settings (connection template). Revenue stays in your store or CRM.

## Slack setup — before delivery
Follow SLACK-SETUP.md (10–15 min pre-work).

1. Create/install a Slack app with bot scope chat:write.
2. Save its token privately in n8n Credentials.
3. Invite the bot to a test channel.
4. Select credential + channel By ID on the Deliver | Slack node.
5. Review the Markdown, then switch on Deliver | Slack. It posts one formatted message per report.

Use the SYNTHETIC demo for screen-sharing. No credentials are included. App installation may require workspace approval.

parameters.content:
## Delivery: choose one or more
All the reports and the AI summary are collected first, then sent to every delivery node you switch on. Leave the others off, or delete them.

- **Slack:** one formatted message per report (emoji title, bold labels, tables as bullet lines). See the Slack setup note.
- **GitHub:** opens a pull request to your personal OS repo with the reports as dated .md files (Settings: githubOwner, githubRepo, githubFolder, githubBase). It creates a new branch each run and never commits to your main branch: you merge the PR. Use a private repo, because reports hold revenue. Needs a GitHub API credential with Contents and Pull requests set to read and write, on the four GitHub nodes.
- **Email:** one email with all the reports in the body and attached (Settings: emailTo).

Set `n8nUrl` in Settings to your n8n address and both email and Slack link back to this workflow and the run.

Incomplete reports are delivered too, so a failed source shows up instead of going quiet.

options.systemMessage:
You write the weekly summary for the marketing team from the facts you are given, and nothing else.

Rules:
1. Every number you write must appear in the facts. You may round to whole numbers. Never calculate a new number.
2. How many reviews ran comes only from reviews.complete_count and reviews.total_count. Name the incomplete ones from reviews.incomplete.
3. A report marked incomplete, or a value that is missing or null, is missing data, not zero. Say it is missing and name the failed step.
4. Keep facts, hypotheses and missing data apart. Label every hypothesis as a hypothesis.
5. Month over month and quarter over quarter come only from trends.mom and trends.qoq. If trends.available is false, say they are unavailable and why.
6. History holds earlier weeks, one row each. Describe a trend across weeks only when history_weeks is at least 3; otherwise say there is not enough history yet.
7. Order sources are not incrementality, event counts are not unique people, email counts are messages not people, and non-renewal revenue is not first-time buyer revenue.
8. A report that starts with SAMPLE DATA, or is listed in sample_data, holds example data, not the business's. Say it is sample data and never present its numbers as the business's results.
9. Plain US English, short lines, no em dashes, no all caps.

Output Markdown with exactly these sections:
## Headline (two lines)
## Month and quarter
## Trends
## Flags
## Working
## Not working
## Missing data
## Check next (at most three items, each tied to a line in a report)

parameters.content:
## Trends and AI summary
**Trends:** last 30 against the prior 30 days and last 90 against the prior 90, computed in code from the totals of four Metorik revenue reports. Switch the four Metorik trend requests on with your Metorik login.

**History:** every run is saved to the n8n Data Table `reporting_agent_history`. Create it first, with columns run_date, period_start, period_end (string), reviews_complete, reviews_total, exec_net, exec_orders (number) and facts_json (string).

**AI summary:** switched off until you add an Anthropic credential to AI | Claude model. It only explains numbers the workflow computed, labels hypotheses, and keeps missing data missing. Its file goes out with the reports.

parameters.content:
## 6. Ads review (optional)
**For:** every Google Ads and Meta campaign graded on value-to-spend, flagged when below target or when CPA runs above 2x its usual level, with a plain call: scale, hold, or investigate.

**Source:** Nick Christensen's ads reporting starter (MIT), from his workshop "Ship ICP-driven ad campaigns and automated monitoring". It ships with his sample campaigns, labelled SAMPLE DATA.

**Switch on:** set `adsEnabled` to true in Settings. While it is false the lane is skipped and nothing about ads is delivered.

**Make it live:** replace the two sample nodes with your own rows in the same fields. Meta: a Facebook Graph API credential (access token with `ads_read`) on the insights edge of `act_<your ad account id>`, and the conversion `action_type` your funnel uses (purchase, lead...). Google Ads: the Google Ads node, an HTTP request, or your Google Ads MCP. Then set the targets at the top of Ads | Analyze.

## 5. Email review (Customer.io)
**For:** emails sent and delivered, human opens and clicks, conversions, unsubscribes, bounces and the top sends, this week against last, plus email capture.
**Connection pattern:** Customer.io App API (running automations, broadcasts and their daily metrics; one segment count for capture) → review → Markdown file → collected with the other reports → delivery.
**Setup:** a Bearer Auth credential with an App API key on the five request nodes; set cioCaptureSegmentId and cioCaptureLabel in Settings. Days are UTC; counts are messages, not people.
